newsitem.title: UK: UK's Rifkind tries to head off Europe revolt.
newsitem.headline: UK's Rifkind tries to head off Europe revolt.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind tried to head off a possible revolt over Europe by members of the Conservative party, saying a mutiny would play straight into the hands of the opposition.
"The vast number of Conservative MPs are very very reasonable people," the minister told BBC radio.
"They know perfectly well the Labour Party are simply interested in trying to exploit any differences for opportunistic electoral reasons," he said.

Some members of parliament (MPs) threatened to withdraw support from the government after Prime Minister John Major on Thursday resisted demands for a full debate on plans for the introduction of a single European currency.

Major triggered the latest unrest within Conservative ranks by refusing to give way to calls for a debate on three documents detailing how a European currency will be introduced and how countries that do not join will be treated.

Rifkind said there was no question of the government trying to suppress debate on the matter, saying parliament would have a full day to discuss European matters before a summit of EU leaders in Dublin next month.
